shared_capability: A single reusable, policy-configured dataset health check that evaluates each registered dataset against its declared freshness threshold and schema contract, reports drift by field, and reports 'unknown' (never 'fresh') for datasets that have never been measured.

distinct_needs.need: Know when the engine_test_runs dataset is stale using a 60-minute threshold, checked before every hotfire review.
Compare each table's schema against its declared contract and report drift by field, so an upstream column rename is caught before a dashboard breaks.
An SLA report on NCR table freshness for the weekly ops review, grouped by owner team, where never-measured datasets show as unknown rather than fresh.
One shared, reusable freshness-check capability to replace three hand-rolled versions, with thresholds held as policy configuration rather than code.

symptoms.symptom: The hotfire review dashboard silently showed three-day-old engine test data.
The BOM cost dashboard broke after an upstream column rename, and the break went unnoticed for days.
The team cannot produce a freshness SLA report for NCR tables, and the request requires that unmeasured datasets not appear fresh.
Three forward deployed engineers built separate freshness checks with different thresholds.

underlying_problem: Data consumers have no shared, configurable mechanism that verifies dataset freshness and schema conformance before decisions depend on the data. Failures stay silent until a person notices a wrong or broken dashboard, and each team builds its own inconsistent checks.
observed_facts: syn-req-001: the hotfire review dashboard silently showed three-day-old engine test data last week (observed in the request text).
syn-req-001: the stakeholder asks for staleness of the engine_test_runs dataset with a 60-minute threshold, checked before every review.
syn-req-002: the BOM cost dashboard broke when an upstream column was renamed, and nobody noticed for days.
syn-req-002: the stakeholder asks for a check that compares each table schema against its declared contract and reports drift by field.
syn-req-003: the stakeholder needs an SLA report on freshness of NCR tables for the weekly ops review, grouped by owner team.
syn-req-003: the stakeholder requires that a never-measured dataset be reported as unknown, not as fresh.
syn-req-004: three forward deployed engineers each hand-rolled dataset freshness checks with different thresholds.
syn-req-004: the stakeholder wants one shared, reusable capability where thresholds are policy configuration, not code.
interpretations: Inference: 001, 003 and 004 are all freshness checks, and 004 asks for the shared capability that 001 and 003 each need in their own context.

Inference: 002 is a schema-contract check, not a freshness check. It belongs in the consolidation because it shares the same engine shape (declared expectation per dataset, evaluated on a schedule, reported with a verdict) and the same failure pattern (silent breakage). It is the weakest fit, and it could be split into a separate capability if the team wants a freshness-only scope.
Inference: the common thread across all four is silent failure. Consumers learn about bad data late, from a broken or misleading dashboard, not from a check.
Inference: 003's requirement that unknown never look fresh and 001's requirement for a threshold before every review imply the same default-to-unknown behavior in the shared capability.
Inference: the policy-configuration requirement in 004 applies to 001 and 003 too, since their thresholds (60 minutes, SLA targets) would otherwise be hard-coded per team.
unknowns: Whether each table in 002 and each dataset in 001 and 003 has a declared schema contract or freshness expectation today. No request states that one exists.
Who owns and approves the threshold policy configuration (the FDEs, the data platform team, or each owner team).
Whether engine_test_runs, the BOM tables, and the NCR tables live on the same data platform, which determines whether one check can reach all of them.
Where the freshness signal comes from (last-updated timestamp, load log, or row max timestamp). No request names a source.
Who receives alerts and in what channel. No request specifies notification.
Whether the 60-minute threshold in 001 applies to all datasets or is specific to engine_test_runs.
Whether 002 should be in this capability or split into a separate schema-drift capability.
How the 'before every review' trigger in 001 should be enforced: a scheduled check, a gate on the dashboard, or a manual step.
Whether the three FDE checks in 004 must be migrated to the shared capability, and whether their existing thresholds are to be preserved.
Priority order across the four requests and the date for a first version. No request states a deadline other than the weekly ops review in 003.

questions.question: Should syn-req-002 (schema-contract drift) be consolidated into the same freshness-and-contract capability as 001, 003 and 004, or scoped as a separate capability? The overlap is strong on the silent-failure pattern and weak on check type.
Who owns and approves the policy configuration for thresholds and SLA targets: the data platform team, the forward deployed engineers, or each owner team?
Do the engine_test_runs, BOM, and NCR datasets all sit on one data platform that the shared check can read, and who can confirm this?
What is the priority order and target date for the four requests, given the weekly ops review in syn-req-003?
